FOREWORD 

This Indian Standtu^d was adopted by tiie Bureau of Indian Standards, after tlie draft finalized by tlie Made- 
up Textiles (Otlier Than Ready-Made Garments) Sectional Committee had been approved by tlie Textile 
Division Council. 

The ‘Water proof covers’ described in lliis specification are made from ‘Cloth Duck Rip Stop, Cotton, 
OG 610 g’ waterproof and intended to cover StoresWehicles lying in the open to protect them from sun 
and rain. 


For the purpose of deciding whetlier a particular requirement of this standard is complied witli, tlie final 
value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance witli 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values {revised)'. The number of significant places retained 
ill the roimded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

TEXTILES — WATERPROOF COVERS 


1 SCOPE 

LI This specification prescribes tlie require¬ 
ments of waterproof cover. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 Indian Suindards listed at Annex A itre nec¬ 
essary adjuncts to Uiis standitrd. 

3 MATERIALS 

3.1 The waterproof covers shall be manufac¬ 
tured from following materials confonning to tlie 
standards indicated against tliem: 

Material Specification 

i) Cloth duck rip stop, cotton, Annex B 

OG,610g 

ii) Polypropylene rope IS 5175:1992 

iii) Cotton sewing thread IS 1720:1978 

iv) Chemically passivated aluminium 

eyelets, Size No. 28 and 30 IS 4084:1978 


4 MANUFACTURE 

4.1 The covers shall be fabricated from olive 
green waterproof and rot proof cotton duck, rip 
stop. 

4.2 The covers shtdl be machine sewn witli cot¬ 
ton sewing tliread confonning to vtu-iety number 
42 of IS 1720 : 1978. The stitching shall be of 
even tension tliroughout witli all loose ends se¬ 
curely fastened. The number of stitches shall not 
be less tlian 2 per cm and tlie needle used for 
stitching shall not be too large to leave holes 
tlirough which water may leak. 

4.3 Joints, if any, shall be in the direction of the 
lengtli of tlie cover and shall be made by laying two 
edges of the fabric one over the other with an 
overlap so that two rows of stitching, not less than 
2.5 cm apart, pass through both layers of the 
fabric as shown in Fig. 1. All seams shall be lapped

4.4 The ends and sides of the covers shall be

be 5 cm wide and tum-in shall be tlie full widtli of tlie

material at tlie sides and botli ends and nine folds at 
tlie corners. These nine folds shall be reduced to five 
by cutting from each comer a piece of 10 cm squiire 
tlius permitting tlie shiinksof tlie eyelets to be securely 
set over tlie washers. 


4.5 Chemically passivated iduminium eyelets of 
size 28 and 30 as per IS 4084 : 1978 shall be 
fitted in a line in tlie centre of tlie hem. The 
holes for tlie eyelets shall be made by punching 
with a small punch, the holes being brought to 
the required size by using a marline spike. 

4.6 The lashings shall be made from 8 mm 
polypropylene rope and shall be spliced to each 
comer eyelet. The free ends of tlie lashings shall 
be suitably heat sealed.

confonii to requirements specified in Table 1, 

5.1.1 However, a tolerance of ± 1 percent on 
lengtli iind widtli of a cover shall be permissible 
provided tlie average dimensions of all covers 
under test are not less tlian tlie specified values.

6 MARKING 

6.1 Each cover shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked witli die following infonnation: 

a) Name of material, 

b) Dimensions of cover, 

c) Indication of source of manufacture, iind 

d) Mondi and year of manufacture. 

6.2 Each bale containing waterproof covers shall 
be legibly miu*ked by stencil using indelible mark¬ 
ing ink/paint showing die following details : 


7.2.1 The bales shall be made up in such a way 
diat its cross section is approximately rechtnguliir 
in shape. 

7.3 The seiims of die bale shall be securely sewn 
widi double jute twine widi not less dian 9 stitches 
per 10,0 cm. While stitching the jute clotJi, care 
should be tiiken to avoid piercing die covers dur¬ 
ing die stitching process. wSufficient jute clodi shall 
be pulled out at each comer to fonn ‘eiirs’ about 
15.0 cm in length. The outside semns of die bale 
shall not be demurred unless specified by purchaser. 

8 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 


a) Quantity packed in die bale, 

b) Moiidi and year of packing, 

c) Indication of source of manufacture, 

d) Lot number, and 

e) Gross mass of bale in kg. 

6.3 BIS Certification Marking 

The covers may also be marked widi die Standard 
Mark. 

6.3.1 The use of die Standard Mark is governed 
by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and 
Regulations made thereunder. The details of 
conditions under which the licence for the use of 
Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from die Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 

7 PACKING 

7.1 Each cover shall be delivered in a new, clean 
and dry condition. 

7.2 All covers shall be packed in accordance widi 
die details given in Table 2. 

Table 2 Packing of Waterproof Covers 


8.1 Lot 

The quantity of waterproof covers delivered to a 
buyer against a despatch note shall constitute a lot. 

8.2 The confonnity of die lot to die requirements 
of die standard shall be detennined on the basis of 
tests ciirried out on die smnple selected from it. 
Unless odierwise agreed to between die buyer and 
die seller, die number of waterproof covers to be 
selected at random from a lot shall be according to 
Table 3. To ensure the randomness of selection, 
mediods given in IS 4905 :1968 shiill be followed.

ANNEX B 
( Clause 3.1) 

REQUIREMENTS OF CLOTH DUCK RIP STOP, COTTON 


B-1 GENERAL 

a) The fabric shall be woven from evenly spun 
59 tex X 3 cotton tliread in warp and 59 tex x 
4 cotton tliread in weft. It shall be unifonnly 
woven in plain weave witli fimi selvedges 
using two tlireads working as one after every 
14 tlireads in warp and after every 7 tlireads 
ill weft. It shall be free from spimiiiig, 
weaving and processing defects. 


b) The fabric shall be unifonnly dyed olive green 
witli any suitable dyestuff and shall be water 
and rotproofed.
